title: Three.js/WebGPU graphical overlay layer for scenes
summary: Proposed approach for clickable tooltips/lore/equipment-info, inline-check triggers, and radar-style HUD elements beyond native Foundry capability: a custom overlay layer built in Three.js, targeting WebGPU and TSL (Three Shading Language).
description: Desire to enhance scenes with interactive elements beyond what Foundry natively offers: click-to-reveal tooltips, lore snippets, character/equipment/mech reminders, inline skill-check triggers with richer presentation than plain enricher text, and radar-like displays on the main battle/campaign map — described generally as 'lots of fun stuff.' The proposed technical approach, stated specifically: a special overlay layer built with Three.js, set up in WebGPU using TSL (Three Shading Language), to allow adding custom graphical layers/elements on top of the existing scene.
sourceContext: User planning message, 2026-08-22 — large worldbuilding/tooling brain-dump.
openSubQuestions: Integration feasibility: Foundry's own canvas is already a PixiJS/WebGL rendering context (confirmed in design/foundry-technical-reference.md's research) — layering a separate Three.js/WebGPU context on top is a real technical question worth investigating before committing, not a given.
Whether a lighter-weight approach (DOM overlay, or working within Foundry's existing canvas/PIXI layers) could deliver the same features with less integration risk.
Which specific interactive features are must-have v1 vs. later polish.
